title: Foundational token rebaseline and chart-contrast workflow
creator: Ava Chen
description: Rebaseline Redwood's core design tokens with an emphasis on: (1) accessible color palettes across light/dark modes and high-density UIs, (2) refined typography scale for dense data tables and chat UIs, (3) compact spacing/radius options for feature-rich surfaces, and (4) a new elevation/shadow system that supports contrast-sensitive charts and overlays. This ticket scopes token decisions, cross-team implementation guidance, and a rollout plan to minimize regressions. Deliverables: updated token spec in Figma, token JSON for the design system, engineering migration notes, component impact matrix for buttons/tables/charts, and a QA checklist for visual regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Design tokens (color/typography/spacing/radius/elevation) exported as final JSON and published to the tokens repo
All primary components (Button, Table, Chart, Card, Modal) accept new tokens via variables and render consistently in light/dark/high-contrast modes
Chart color ramps pass WCAG AA for key data contrast pairs at common sizes
Migration guide and at least two sample PRs (buttons and charts) created and approved
No visual regressions flagged in the critical-product-path Percy snapshots after rollout
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Publish token spec to tokens repo and create feature branch; Phase 2: Integrate tokens for Button and Card components with canary visual tests; Phase 3: Apply chart contrast ramp and run data-visual QA; Phase 4: Broad component migration and update Console themes; Phase 5: Monitor metrics and revertable release for 2 weeks. Each phase includes a smoke test and a rollback plan.
qa_checklist: Render components in light, dark, and high-contrast modes
Run Percy visual snapshots on component PRs and compare to baseline
Validate chart color pairs against WCAG contrast tool (links in Confluence)
Verify typography scale at 12/13/14/16/18/20 for mobile and desktop breakpoints
Confirm spacing tokens produce no layout regression in data table dense mode
tradeoffs: Higher contrast ramps reduce color vibrancy; chosen balance favors legibility for data-critical UIs
Compact spacing improves information density but increases touch-target trade-offs on mobile; we keep a separate touch-spacing token set for mobile where needed
Simpler elevation system (fewer discrete elevations) reduces cognitive overhead for engineers but requires careful shadow opacity tuning to maintain depth cues across monitors
